name: Texas Is the Reason
label: Revelation
lede: Nine songs, one album, a Misfits lyric for a name and a band that broke up in Germany on the eve of a Capitol deal, which is how the record became Revelation's best seller instead of a major-label debut.

eras.title: Krishnacore kids go melodic
eras.text: The two founders came out of the most devout corner of hardcore: Norman Brannon had played guitar in Shelter as Norman Arenas, Chris Daly had drummed in 108. With a singer from Copper and a bassist, they made something warmer and more open-ended, and New York clubs started booking them as the opener everybody showed up early for.

years.h: A Misfits lyric, a Kennedy theory, a band
years.p: Brannon and Daly add bassist [[Scott Winegard|400a7302-6a36-4c80-b5fc-17d3d0d4e3cf]] and singer-guitarist [[Garrett Klahn|f6190334-6d61-473a-9992-c4791da7adc6]]. [[Chris Leo|df1ce5f2-cfb5-4c81-84b6-4a4e9a6a5927]] of [[The Van Pelt|4ce909db-0da6-4eed-bfe6-6c1f71e265b0]] suggests the name, lifted from a [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]] song and pointing at the JFK conspiracy theories.
years.xp:
Revelation's bio traces the members back through Shelter, 108 and Resurrection, a family tree of early-'90s hardcore that sounds nothing like the band they became.

Brannon was still Norman Arenas then, and edited the zine Anti-Matter. He changed his surname legally in 2004, and has written that almost everyone mispronounced Arenas.

years.p: The debut EP makes them headliners almost immediately.
A shared single on Simba Recordings and Art Monk Construction, the kind of small-run record that got passed around at shows.

[[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] co-produces the album with the band, and Drew Mazurek engineers. The songs are already road-tested.

eras.title: Do you know who you are?
eras.text: One full-length, nine songs, under forty minutes. The title came from the words John Lennon was reportedly asked before he died, Klahn was 21, and major labels were already calling.

years.h: Do You Know Who You Are? · Revelation
years.p: Mastered by Vlad Meller at Sony Music Studios, sleeve by Glenn Maryansky. It becomes Revelation's best-selling release, and ends up on best-of lists from Rolling Stone, LA Weekly and NME.
years.xp:
Spin, Alternative Press and Paste all later put it among the essential records of the '90s. Critics kept coming back to Klahn's voice, warm without taking over.

It was the only album the band ever made.
play: Do You Know Who You Are?

years.p: Two of the bands that would define '90s emo on one piece of vinyl.
Major labels chase the band through a year of heavy touring. Capitol wins.

eras.title: Eight hundred Germans and a way out
eras.text: About ten months after the album came out, the band stopped. It happened on a European tour, with the Capitol deal waiting at home, and the members have told it as a clean decision rather than a blowup.

q: There were eight hundred Germans singing along with us.
years.p: The final show is in Bielefeld. Brannon remembers the crowd singing every word, looking over at Daly, and knowing it was done.
years.xp:
Klahn's version, told to Paste: the band had agreed that if that night's show was great, they'd call it there. The split came at Frankfurt airport, with the Capitol deal set for the next day in his telling.

Wikipedia has them touring Europe before signing with Capitol. Either way, there was no major-label album. Daly went on to [[Jets to Brazil|675ec992-a8e4-41f8-b28b-1aad0c8a9ad1]] with [[Blake Schwarzenbach|c7d68007-b688-426f-a496-08467a0a6f44]]; Klahn formed New Rising Sons.

eras.title: Anniversaries only
eras.text: The reunions came on round numbers and sold out fast. Each one was pitched as a last time, and each time the band came back.

years.h: Ten years on: two sold-out nights at Irving Plaza
years.p: The first reunion, back in New York, for the album's tenth anniversary.

years.h: Irving Plaza and Music Hall of Williamsburg
years.p: Another New York run, sixteen years after the album.
Revelation remasters everything and adds two previously unreleased songs. A limited North American tour follows.

years.h: A final reunion show at the Electric Ballroom, London
Twenty years on: Saint Vitus, Brooklyn
years.p: A sold-out show at the small Brooklyn metal bar for the album's twentieth anniversary. A second night gets added.

At the TLA in Philadelphia, the band joins a benefit for the late [[Sense Field|8d7bf045-1526-404d-b37c-6f49b714d614]] and [[Further Seems Forever|2bc3d11f-58fe-4adb-bfd9-6d316973005a]] singer, raising money for his son's college fund. Klahn and Richie Birkenhead are on the bill with [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] and a reunited Sense Field.

eras.title: Nine months in a room
eras.text: This time the band rehearsed for most of a year before telling anyone, then went further than it ever had in the '90s. It went without one founder, who explained why on his own terms.

years.p: Klahn says they spent nine or ten months in a room getting the fourteen songs right, without telling anybody.
Brannon says revisiting the band means revisiting his mid-'90s life as a closeted gay man, and he doesn't want to. He adds there's no bad blood. John Herguth plays guitar.
The reunited band plays the Las Vegas festival at the Downtown Las Vegas Events Center, October 10–12, on a bill with reunions from Rilo Kiley and Minus the Bear.

years.h: Places they never got to in 1997
years.p: The run takes them to Australia and Japan for the first time, to Primavera Sound, and onto dates with [[Jimmy Eat World|bbc5b66b-d037-4f26-aecf-0b129e7f876a]] and [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]]. No new songs planned, Klahn says, unless they come naturally.
